titleEn: The Secret History of the Mongols — §§218–223: Sorqan-Shira, Naya'a and the Thousands
about: The rewards of 1206 go on. Chinggis Qahan makes good on old debts: Narin-To'oril is told to gather his scattered Nekus kinsmen (§218); Sorqan-Shira, who hid the boy Temüjin among the Taichi'ud, is offered a favour and asks for a free camp on the Selenge, which he gets, with freedom from penalty nine times over, Chila'un and Chimbai are told to name what they lack, and Sorqan-Shira, Badai and Kishiliq are given the rule of the spoils of war and the hunt (§219); Naya'a, who set his captive lord Tarqutai-Kiriltuq free before coming over, is praised for it and given the middle ten thousand, while Bo'orchu and Muqali take the right and left (§220); then thousands are formed for Jebe and Sübegetei (§221), for Degei the shepherd (§222) and for Küchügur and Mulqalqu (§223). Grammar to watch: long chains of converbs ending in -žu/-žü, the polite plural command in -dqun, the reflexive-possessive endings (-jen, -ban, -jan, -ben), and speech set inside speech, often with no quotation marks in Shiratori.

sentences.t: Basa Čiṅgis Qaγan Čaγan-Γoγ̇a-jin köġün Narin-Toγ̇ori- l-a ügülerün:
sentences.l: Again Chinggis Qaγan, Čaγan-Γoγ̇a-of son Narin-Toγ̇oril-to saying:
sentences.i: Again Chinggis Qahan said to Narin-To'oril, the son of Chagan-Go'a:
sentences.n: Narin-Toγ̇ori- and l-a are one name broken at the line end: Narin-Toγ̇oril, with the dative-locative -a (Ming 行), 'to'. ügülerün is ügüle- 'to speak' with the time converb -rün, 'when saying', which the Secret History uses to bring in speech. Čaγan-Γoγ̇a-jin is the father's name in the genitive (-jin after a vowel; Ming 的), set before köġün 'son'. The reading Narin-To'oril is mine from the break; the same man is called plain Toγ̇oril below.

morph.gloss: Chinggis, the title borne by Temüjin from 1206 [太祖︀]
Narin-To'oril, a man's name (first half, broken at the line end: Narin-Toγ̇ori-l-a) [人名]
the last letter of the name, completing Toγ̇oril

sentences.t: "Ečige čin-u Čaγan-Γoγ̇a min-u emüne kičiġežü qadqulduqu bolun
sentences.l: "Father your Čaγan-Γoγ̇a me-of before careful-ing, fighting-one becoming,
sentences.i: “Your father Chagan-Go'a, taking care in front of me and being one who fights,
sentences.n: Shiratori's opening quotation mark comes at Ečige and the speech runs to abtuγai. Read čin-u as 'your' (či 'you' + genitive -u on the stem čin-), standing between ečige 'father' and the name, so 'your father Chagan-Go'a'; min-u emüne is 'of me, in front', i.e. 'before me'. kičiġežü is kičiġe- 'to take care, be careful' (Ming 謹愼着, 'being careful') + converb -žü; qadqulduqu is qadqul- 'to fight' + the reciprocal -du- + the participle -qu (Ming 厮殺的, 'fighting'), and bolun is bol- + converb -un, 'being'. The clause is a converb chain that runs on to the verb in the next unit; 'being one who fights' is the plain grammar of qadqulduqu bolun; what it says of the father (that he was a fighter, or was fighting there) the words leave open.

morph.gloss: genitive on the stem čin-: your
genitive: of, set after its noun
to take care, be careful [謹︀愼着]

sentences.i: at Dalan-Baljut, in the time of fighting, was killed by Jamuqa.
sentences.n: The verb at last: alaγdaluγ̇a is ala- 'to kill' + the passive -γda- + a past ending -luγ̇a (Ming 被殺了來, 'was killed'). The passive takes its doer in the dative-locative, so Žamuqa-da (Ming 行) is 'by Jamuqa'. Dalan-Balžud-ta is the place with the dative-locative -ta, after a consonant (Ming 地面行). qadqulduqui-dur is the same stem as before (with the reciprocal -du-) with the participle -qui and -dur, 'at the time of fighting'.

morph.gloss: Jamuqa, a man's name [人名 行]
dative-locative: by, to (agent of a passive)

sentences.t: Edöġe Toγ̇oril ečige-jüġen tusa önöčid-ün abliγa abtuγai"
sentences.l: Now Toγ̇oril father-own favour forlorn-of grant let-receive"
sentences.i: Now let To'oril receive, for his own father, a favour, a grant for the forlorn.”
sentences.n: The closing quotation mark ends Chagan-Go'a's story. This line is hard and I have read it only from the words: tusa (Ming 恩, 'favour') and abliγa (Ming 受賜, 'what is given') are both nouns, önöčid-ün is 'of the forlorn' (Ming 孤獨(每)的, with önöči of uncertain stem), and ečige-jüġen has the reflexive-possessive -jüġen, 'his own father'. abtuγai is ab- 'to take, receive' + the optative -tuγai (Ming 者), 'let (him) receive'. The word order suggests that the favour owed to the father is to pass to the forlorn son; that is a guess.

morph.gloss: the forlorn, solitary one [孤獨(每)的]
a share or grant received [受賜]

sentences.i: Being told this, To'oril said:
sentences.n: keġegdežü is keġe- 'to say' + the passive -gde- + converb -žü: 'being told' (Ming 被說着). So the one addressed in the speech just ended hears it and answers; Toγ̇oril here is Narin-Toγ̇oril above, shortened.

sentences.t: "Sojurγaγ̇asu Neküs aqa deġü min-u qari tutum buratara bi.
sentences.l: "Favour-if-you-show, Neküs elder-brother younger-brother my tribe each scattered are.
sentences.i: “If you show favour, my Nekus kinsmen, elder and younger brothers, tribe by tribe, are scattered.
sentences.n: sojurγaγ̇asu is sojurγa- 'to show favour' + the conditional -γ̇asu (Ming 恩賜呵; the Ming's 呵 marks 'if, when'). Neküs (Ming 種(名)) is a clan name; aqa deġü, 'elder brother, younger brother', is a pair meaning 'brothers, kinsmen'. min-u comes before qari (Ming 部落, 'tribe, band') this time, and tutum (Ming 每裏, 'each') after it, so 'my … each band'. buratara is a stem with -tara and Ming 漫散, 'scattered'; the verb is bi (Ming 有), 'is'. Shiratori opens a new quotation at Sojurγaγ̇asu.

morph.gloss: to show favour, bestow a grace [恩賜呵]
the Nekus, a clan name [種(名)]
scattered (stem not analysed; Ming 漫散) [漫散]

sentences.t: Sojurγaγ̇asu Neküs aqa deġü-jüġen čiγ̇ulγa- suγai"
sentences.l: Favour-if-you-show, Neküs elder-brother younger-brother-own gathering let-me."
sentences.i: If you show favour, let me gather my own Nekus kinsmen, elder and younger brothers.”
sentences.n: Two words are cut at the line end in a way that matters: čiγ̇ulγa- and suγai make one word, čiγ̇ulγasuγai, from čiγ̇ul- 'to gather' + the causative -γa- + the first-person optative -suγai, 'let me' (Ming 我). deġü-jüġen is deġü with the reflexive-possessive and, I think, the accusative, 'his own younger brother(s)'. The closing quotation mark ends To'oril's speech.

morph.gloss: to show favour, bestow a grace [恩賜]
the Nekus, a clan name [種(名)]
to gather, assemble (stem inferred from the Ming 聚) [敎(聚)]

sentences.i: When he had said this, Chinggis Qahan issued a decree:
sentences.n: keġeġesü is keġe- 'to say' + the conditional -ġesü (Ming 說呵); in a story it comes out as 'when he had said'. žarliγ bolurun is the set phrase 'decree … when becoming', rendered 'issued a decree'; bolurun is bol- + the time converb -urun.

morph.gloss: Chinggis, the title borne by Temüjin from 1206 [太祖︀]

sentences.i: “That being so, gather your own Nekus kinsmen, elder and younger brothers,
sentences.n: Tein böġesü is a standing opener, 'so, it being so' (tein, Ming 那般, 'that way', and böġesü, 'if it is'; Ming 有呵). deġü-ġen has the reflexive-possessive -ġen (Ming 自的行), here 'your own younger brother', where the same man had said -jüġen above. čiγ̇ulγažu is the causative converb, 'making gather'. A new opening mark appears at Tein.

morph.gloss: the Nekus, a clan name [種(名)]
to gather, assemble (stem inferred from the Ming 聚) [敎聚着]

sentences.t: či uruγ-un uruγ-a kürtele medežü ülü-ü aqu"
sentences.l: you offspring-of offspring-to until managing not? is-there?"
sentences.i: you shall have them in your charge down to the offspring of your offspring, shall you not?”
sentences.n: či is 'you' (singular); uruγ-un uruγ-a kürtele, 'to the offspring of the offspring, until', is a formula for 'down to the latest descendants' (uruγ 'offspring' + genitive -un, then uruγ + dative -a; kür- 'to reach' + -tele 'until'). medežü is mede- 'to know' with the Ming sense 管着, 'having charge of'. ülü-ü aqu is the awkward end: ülü is 'not', and the Ming gives a question (有麽, 'is there?'). I read it as a rhetorical 'shall you not?'; that is a guess.

morph.gloss: to know; here to have charge of [管着]

sentences.i: so saying, he issued a decree.
sentences.n: keġen is keġe- 'to say' with the converb -n, the usual closing of a speech (Ming 麽道); žarliγ bolba, 'made a decree', is the plain past of the phrase seen above.

sentences.i: Again Chinggis Qahan said to Sorqan-Shira:
sentences.n: The same opening as before: ügüle- 'to speak' + the time converb -rün, with the dative-locative -da (Ming 行) on the name, 'to Sorqan-Shira'.

morph.gloss: Chinggis, the title borne by Temüjin from 1206 [太祖︀]

sentences.t: "Nama-ji üčügen čaγ-tur Taičiγ̇ud-un Tarqutai-Kiriltuγ aqa deġü-de naitažu bariγ̇asu
sentences.l: "Me small time-at, Taičiγ̇ud-of Tarqutai-Kiriltuγ elder-brother younger-brother-to envying, when-he-seized
sentences.i: “When I was small, Tarqutai-Kiriltuq of the Taichi'ud, envying (his) brothers, seized me,
sentences.n: Chinggis recalls his boyhood; Shiratori's opening quotation mark is on Nama-ji and the speech runs on to ta, in the offer of favour below. nama-ji is bi 'I' on the stem nama- with the accusative -ji (Ming 我行), 'me', object of bariγ̇asu 'when he seized' (bari- 'to seize' + the conditional -γ̇asu; Ming 拿了呵). čaγ-tur is 'at the time' (dative-locative -tur after a back vowel), so üčügen čaγ-tur is 'when small'. naitažu is a converb of a verb 'to envy' (Ming 嫉妒着). The dative-locative on aqa deġü-de is the awkward part: I read it as the thing envied, 'envying the brothers', but who envies whom is not clear from the words alone, and the next unit turns the envy round.

morph.gloss: accusative: me, as object (after a vowel)
to envy, be jealous (stem inferred from the Ming 嫉妒) [嫉妒着]
to seize, take hold of [拿了呵]

sentences.i: and there, saying that he was being envied by his own brothers,
sentences.n: naitaγdamu is naita- 'to envy' + the passive -γda- + the present -mu (Ming 被嫉妒有, 'is envied'); the doer stands in the dative-locative, aqa deġü-deġen with the reflexive-possessive, 'by his own brothers'. keġen closes it, 'saying'. The words are plain, but how this clause hangs on the sentence before it is my reading; the Ming gives no hint beyond 'so saying'. The subject of 'is envied' is not marked, and whose words these are I cannot say; `i` gives them as reported speech.

morph.gloss: dative-locative with reflexive-possessive: by one's own
to envy (stem inferred from the Ming 嫉妒) [被嫉妒 有]

sentences.t: Sorγan-Šira Čilaγ̇un, Čimbai köġud(i)-jer(i)-jen Qadaγ̇an-i ökin(i)-jen asaraγ̇ulžu miγ̇užu ažu
sentences.l: Sorγan-Šira, Čilaγ̇un, Čimbai sons-with-own, Qadaγ̇an (acc) daughter-own having-caused-to-raise, hiding, staying,
sentences.i: Sorqan-Shira, with his own sons Chila'un and Chimbai, having Qada'an, his own daughter, tend (me); hiding (me), staying (with me),
sentences.n: A converb chain (asaraγ̇ulžu, miγ̇užu, ažu, each '…ing') with the doers named first. köġud(i)-jer(i)-jen is one word: köġü- 'son' + plural -d, then -jer, an ending shaped like the instrumental 'with', then the reflexive-possessive -jen (the (i)s are Shiratori's), 'with his own sons'. Qadaγ̇an-i is a woman's name with the accusative -i (Ming 行); ökin(i)-jen is 'his own daughter'. asaraγ̇ulžu is asara- 'to look after' with the causative -γ̇ul-, 'having caused to be raised' (Ming 敎擡擧着), the object ('me') understood. miγ̇užu: the Ming character 你 reads ni-, so the stem is niγu- 'to hide' (Ming 藏着). Qadaγ̇an-i and ökin(i)-jen take the accusative, so Qada'an is the one made to tend (the object of the causative), not a doer beside the sons; the doers of the whole chain are Sorqan-Shira and his sons. That the one tended and hidden is Temüjin, left unnamed, is my reading.

morph.gloss: ending shaped like the instrumental: with
Qada'an, a woman's name [女名 行]
to look after, rear [敎擡擧着]
to hide (printed miγu-; the Ming 你 reads ni-) [藏着]

sentences.i: you let me go, and came, indeed, you.
sentences.n: nama-ji is 'me' again (accusative), the object of talbižu (talbi- 'to set down, let go' + converb -žu; Ming 放着). irebe-že is ire- 'to come' + past -be + the particle -že, 'indeed' (Ming 來了也者). The sentence closes on ta, 'you' (plural polite, Ming 您), set after the verb to name the doer, so the whole chain above is addressed to Sorqan-Shira.

morph.gloss: accusative: me, as object (after a vowel)
to set down, let go [放着]

sentences.t: Tere tusa sain-i tan-u sedkižü qara süni žeġüdün-dür
sentences.l: That favour good-(acc) your thinking, black night dream-in,
sentences.i: Thinking of that kindness of yours, the good, in the black night, in dreams,
sentences.n: tere tusa is 'that favour'; sain-i is sain 'good' with the accusative -i (Ming 好行), as the thing thought of; tan-u is 'your' (ta, stem tan-, + genitive -u), set after the noun it qualifies, as min-u is. sedkižü is sedki- 'to think' + converb -žü. The two time phrases run on into the next unit: qara süni 'black night', žeġüdün-dür 'in a dream', dative-locative -dür (Ming 夢裏).

sentences.t: gegeġen üdür čeġeži-dür sedkižü jabuba-že bi.
sentences.l: bright day breast-in thinking, I-went-about-indeed, I.
sentences.i: and in the bright day, in my breast, thinking (of it), I went about, indeed.
sentences.n: gegeġen üdür, 'bright day', answers qara süni, 'black night', in the unit before; čeġeži-dür is the dative-locative of čeġeži, which I take as 'breast' (Ming 心懷, 'heart, bosom'; an earlier part glossed the same word 胷膈, 'chest, diaphragm'), the seat of thought. jabuba-že is jabu- 'to walk, go about' + past -ba + particle -že (Ming 行了也者), 'I went about, indeed'. The subject bi 'I' is set last, as ta was.

morph.gloss: to walk, go about [行了 也者︀]

sentences.t: Ta že na-dur Taičiγ̇ud-ača udaγ̇an-a irebe-že.
sentences.l: You yet me-to Taičiγ̇ud-from late-to came-indeed.
sentences.i: You, however, came to me late, from the Taichi'ud.
sentences.n: že here stands after ta (Ming 卻, 'but, yet'), a particle of contrast rather than the 'indeed' of irebe-že. na-dur is bi 'I' on the stem na- with the dative-locative -dur, 'to me' (Ming 我行). Taičiγ̇ud-ača is the ablative, 'from the Taichi'ud'. udaγ̇an-a is udaγ̇an 'slow, late' with -a (Ming 遲行), 'late'.

sentences.t: Edöġe bi tan-i sojurγaγ̇asu ambar sojurγal taγ̇alaqun ta" keġebe.
sentences.l: Now I you-(acc) favour-if-I-show, what favour pleasing you," he-said.
sentences.i: Now, if I show favour to you, what favour is pleasing to you?” he said.
sentences.n: Chinggis's offer, and the closing quotation mark of the speech Shiratori opened at Nama-ji. tan-i is ta on the stem tan- with the accusative -i (Ming 您行); sojurγaγ̇asu is the conditional of sojurγa- 'to show favour', as above. ambar is a word I cannot find elsewhere; the Ming reads 怎生, 'how, what', and I follow it. taγ̇alaqun is a guess: taγ̇ala- 'to be fond of, like' (Ming 愛) with an ending -qun of uncertain force (compare -dqun, the polite plural imperative). The sense 'what favour pleases you' rests on the Ming alone.

morph.gloss: to show favour, bestow a grace [恩賜呵]
what, how (Ming 怎生; sense uncertain) [怎生]
to be fond of, like (stem inferred from the Ming 愛) [愛每]

sentences.t: Sorγan-Šira Čilaγ̇un, Čimbai köġud(i)-jer(i)-jen bolun ügülerün:
sentences.l: Sorγan-Šira, Čilaγ̇un, Čimbai sons-with-own being, saying:
sentences.i: Sorqan-Shira, together with his sons Chila'un and Chimbai, said:
sentences.n: köġud(i)-jer(i)-jen is the same word as in the earlier chain, 'with his own sons'; bolun (bol- 'to become, be' + converb -un, Ming 做) means here 'being' (together). That the three speak together, or that Sorqan-Shira speaks for them, is not decided by the grammar; the verb is singular in sense, and the speech uses 'I' (-su).

morph.gloss: ending shaped like the instrumental: with

sentences.i: “If you show favour, let me be free in my camp.
sentences.n: darqalasu is darqala- 'to be free' (Ming 自在, 'at ease, at liberty') + -su, the first-person optative (Ming 我), 'let me be free'; compare -suγai in čiγ̇ulγasuγai. nutuγ is 'camp, home pasture'; its case is not marked, so 'in my camp' is a reading, not a form.

morph.gloss: to show favour, bestow a grace [恩賜呵]
to be free, at liberty (stem inferred from the Ming 自在) [自在我]

sentences.i: Camping in the land of the Merkid, on the Selenge, let me be free.
sentences.n: Merkid-ün γažar is 'land of the Merkid' (genitive -ün after a consonant, Ming 的). Seleṅge-ji, the river name with -ji (Ming 行), is the place of camping; the form is the accusative or an old locative, so 'on the Selenge' is the sense, not a parsing. nutuγlažu is nutuγla- 'to camp' + converb -žu (Ming 營盤做着).

morph.gloss: the Merkid, a people [種(名) 的]
Selenge, a river name [地名 行]
to camp, occupy as pasture [營盤做着]
to be free, at liberty [自在我]

sentences.t: Basa busu sojurγal Čiṅgis Qaγan medetügei" keġebe.
sentences.l: Again other favour Chinggis Qaγan let-know," he-said.
sentences.i: As for any other favour, let Chinggis Qahan know (it),” he said.
sentences.n: busu sojurγal is 'other favour' (busu, Ming 別, 'other'). medetügei is mede- 'to know' + the optative -tügei, 'let him know' (Ming 知也者); I take it as 'let him decide', but the word is 'know'. The closing quotation mark ends Sorqan-Shira's speech, opened at Sojurγaγ̇asu above (the speech opened at Nama-ji closed at ta).

morph.gloss: Chinggis, the title borne by Temüjin from 1206 [太祖︀]

sentences.i: Then Chinggis Qahan said:
sentences.n: Teġün-dür is the oblique stem of tere 'that' with the dative-locative -dür (Ming 那的裏), 'thereupon'.

morph.gloss: Chinggis, the title borne by Temüjin from 1206 [太祖︀]

sentences.t: "Merkid-ün γažar Seleṅge-ji nutuγlažu nutuγ ba darqaladqun kü.
sentences.l: "Merkid-of land Selenge (acc) camping, camp and be-free indeed.
sentences.i: “Camping in the land of the Merkid, on the Selenge, be free, camp and all, indeed.
sentences.n: The first half repeats Sorqan-Shira's request. nutuγ ba darqaladqun kü is harder: ba (Ming 并) is 'and, also', kü (Ming 也) an emphatic 'indeed', and darqaladqun is darqala- with -dqun, the polite plural imperative (Ming 您), 'be free (you all)'. So 'be free, camp and all' is a reading; 'and your camp too' is as likely.

morph.gloss: the Merkid, a people [種(名) 的]
Selenge, a river name [地名 行]
to camp, occupy as pasture [營盤做着]
to be free, at liberty [自在您]

sentences.t: Uruγ-un uruγ-a kürtele qorčilaγ̇ulžu ötögleġülžü darqaladqun.
sentences.l: Offspring-of offspring-to until bow-and-quiver-bearing-causing, cup-offering-causing, be-free.
sentences.i: Down to the offspring of your offspring, having (them) bear the bow and offer the cup, be free.
sentences.n: uruγ-un uruγ-a kürtele is the formula 'down to the latest descendants' met earlier. qorčilaγ̇ulžu is qorčila- 'to bear the bow and quiver' (from qorči 'quiver-bearer') with the causative -γ̇ul- and converb -žu; ötögleġülžü is ötögle- 'to offer the cup' (Ming 喝盞) in the same form. Both stems are inferred from the Ming 敎帶弓箭着 and 敎喝盞着. They name privileges of rank, as I read them, but the text does not say so.

morph.gloss: to bear the bow and quiver (stem inferred from the Ming) [敎帶弓箭着]
to offer the cup (stem inferred from the Ming 喝盞) [敎喝︀盞着]
to be free, at liberty [自在您]

sentences.i: Nine times, let them not enter into penalty or guilt.”
sentences.n: jesün is 'nine' (Ming 九次, 'nine times'); aldal-dur and ereġü-dür are two nouns, 'penalty' (Ming 罰) and 'guilt' (Ming 罪), each in the dative-locative, 'into'. bu orotuγai is the prohibitive bu with oro- 'to enter' + the optative -tuγai (Ming 休入者), 'let (them) not enter'. Shiratori prints no closing mark here, and his only closing mark for this stretch is at γuidqun, many lines later; the closing mark in `i` is supplied, and `i` opens a fresh one at erte below. 'Nine' is probably a round number for 'again and again', as I read it.

sentences.i: so saying, he issued a decree.
sentences.n: The closing formula, as in §218.

sentences.t: Basa Čiṅgis Qaγan Čilaγ̇un, Čimbai qojar-i sojurγarun
sentences.l: Again Chinggis Qaγan, Čilaγ̇un, Čimbai two (acc) when-showing-favour,
sentences.i: Again, when Chinggis Qahan showed favour to the two, Chila'un and Chimbai,
sentences.n: Basa is printed with a different first character here (Ming 再 again; Shiratori's 巴徹 for the usual 巴撒), a variant spelling of the same word. qojar-i is qojar 'two' with the accusative -i (Ming 兩箇行), 'the two'; sojurγarun is sojurγa- 'to show favour' with the time converb -run, 'when showing favour' (Ming 恩賜時). There is no colon; the speech follows in the next unit.

morph.gloss: Chinggis, the title borne by Temüjin from 1206 [太祖︀]
to show favour, bestow a grace [恩賜時]

sentences.t: erte Čilaγ̇un, Čimbai qojar-un ügülegsen üges sedkižü ker qandaqu ta.
sentences.l: Earlier Čilaγ̇un, Čimbai two-of having-spoken words thinking, how to-be-fulfilled, you.
sentences.i: “Earlier, thinking of the words the two, Chila'un and Chimbai, had spoken: how is it to be fulfilled, you?
sentences.n: Shiratori has no opening quotation mark here, though his closing mark comes at the end of the speech (at γuidqun, below); `i` supplies the opening mark at erte. erte (Ming 在前) is 'before, earlier'. ügülegsen üges is the past participle of ügüle- + the plural of üge 'word': 'the words spoken'. qojar-un is 'of the two'. ker qandaqu ta is the hard end: ker 'how' (Ming 怎), qandaqu from a stem I take as qanda- 'to be complete, fulfilled' (Ming 滿立的, 'full-standing'; the stem is uncertain), with the participle -qu: 'how is it to be made good?'.

morph.gloss: early, before, in former times [在前]
to be full, be fulfilled (stem uncertain; Ming 滿立) [滿立的]

sentences.t: Čilaγ̇un, Čimbai ta qojar sedkil(i)-jen ügüledkün böġesü
sentences.l: Čilaγ̇un, Čimbai you two heart-own if-you-say,
sentences.i: You two, Chila'un and Chimbai, if you say what is in your own heart,
sentences.n: ta qojar, 'you two', follows the two names. sedkil(i)-jen is sedkil 'heart, mind' with the reflexive-possessive. ügüledkün is ügüle- 'to speak' with -dkün, the polite plural ending of command; but here it is followed by böġesü, 'if it be', and the Ming (說的每有呵) reads it as 'if you say'. So the ending is doing the work of a participle before böġesü; the analysis is tentative.

morph.gloss: polite plural ending (here 'you say', before böġesü)

sentences.i: if you ask for what you lack,
sentences.n: dataγ̇ui-ban is the word dutaγ̇u 'lacking' (spelled with a- here; Ming 缺少; compare dutaγ̇u-juγ̇an below) with an ending -i of uncertain force and -ban, the reflexive-possessive, here an accusative: 'one's own lack'. γuiqun is γui- 'to ask for, beg' (Ming 索) with an ending -qun, again before böġesü, 'if you ask'.

morph.gloss: lacking, wanting (from duta- 'to lack'; printed dataγ̇u-; as in the glossary's dutaγ̇u) [缺少 自的行]
ending (uncertain; perhaps the accusative, perhaps part of the stem)

sentences.i: do not tell it to someone in between.
sentences.n: žaγ̇ura, 'between' (Ming 其間), with küġün-e, 'to a man' (küġün is 'person', not köġün 'son'), is, I think, a go-between: do not send word through another. The next unit supports this by asking them to speak in person. bu keleledkün is the prohibitive bu + kelele- 'to speak, tell' (kele 'tongue' + verb) with -dkün, here a polite plural; the pair bu … -dkün as a negative command is a reading.

sentences.t: Oġer-ün bejes(i)-jer ama-γ̇ar na-dur ta öġesüd sedkigsen(i)-jen keleledkün;
sentences.l: Own persons-with, mouth-with, me-to you selves having-thought-own say;
sentences.i: In your own persons, by mouth, tell me yourselves what you have thought;
sentences.n: Two instrumentals (the case of 'with, by means of'), side by side: öġer-ün bejes(i)-jer, 'with one's own persons' (öġer 'own' + genitive -ün; beje 'body, person' + plural -s, the (i) Shiratori's; Ming 親身), and ama-γ̇ar, 'by mouth' (Ming 口). na-dur is 'to me' (Ming 我行). öġesüd is öġesün 'self' with the plural -d. sedkigsen(i)-jen is the past participle of sedki- 'to think' with the reflexive-possessive, 'what one has thought', the object of keleledkün 'tell (you all)'. The sense is: speak to me yourselves, not through others.

morph.gloss: to think [想了的 自的行]

sentences.t: dutaγ̇u-juγ̇an öġesün γuidqun" keġen žarliγ bolba.
sentences.l: lack-own yourselves ask-for," saying decree he-made.
sentences.i: and ask for what you lack, yourselves.” So saying, he issued a decree.
sentences.n: dutaγ̇u-juγ̇an is the stem 'to lack' as a noun with the reflexive-possessive after a vowel, -juγ̇an, 'one's own lack'; öġesün is 'oneself'; γuidqun is γui- 'to ask for' with -dqun, the polite plural command (Ming 索您). The closing quotation mark is Shiratori's; it ends the speech whose opening `i` has supplied at erte.

morph.gloss: to lack (stem inferred from the Ming 缺少) [缺少的 自的行]

sentences.i: Again: “Sorqan-Shira, Badai, Kishiliq, you, as free men,
sentences.n: Shiratori's opening mark comes at Sorγan-Šira, so Basa stays outside the speech. darqad is darqan 'a free man' (Ming 自在, 'free, at ease') with the plural -d, 'the free ones'; as in the glossary's darqad-un, any technical sense of darqan is not in the sources. Chinggis names three men: Sorqan-Shira, Badai and Kishiliq.

morph.gloss: a free man (Ming 自在, 'free, at ease'; as in the glossary's darqad-un) [自在每]

sentences.t: basa darqalarun olon daisun-dur qaγ̇ulžu olža oluγ̇asu oluγsaγ̇ar abudqun.
sentences.l: and again when-you-are-made-free, many enemies-at routing, booty if-you-get, what-you-got-by take.
sentences.i: and again, when you are set free, routing many enemies, if you get booty, take it according to what you have got.
sentences.n: basa darqalarun: darqala- 'to be free, to make free' with the time converb -run (Ming 敎自在時, 'when (I) cause you to be free'). olon daisun-dur is 'to many enemies' (daisun 'enemy' + dative-locative -dur, Ming 敵行); qaγ̇ulžu is qaγ̇ul- 'to rout' + converb, 'routing, attacking'. oluγ̇asu is ol- 'to get' + conditional (Ming 得呵); oluγsaγ̇ar is the past participle oluγsan with the instrumental -γ̇ar, 'by what was got' (Ming 依着, 'according to'); abudqun is ab- 'to take' + -dqun, the polite plural command. So the rule: you keep what you take.

morph.gloss: to be free, make free [敎自在時]
to get, find [得的 依着]

sentences.i: If you hunt wild beasts, take according to what you have killed.”
sentences.n: Oroγ̇a göreġesün-dür: göreġesün is 'game, wild beasts' (Ming 獸 行, dative-locative -dür), oroγ̇a (Ming 野) 'wild'. abalaγ̇asu is abala- 'to hunt in a drive' (stem inferred from the Ming 圍獵) + the conditional; alaγsaγ̇ar is ala- 'to kill' + the past participle -γsan + instrumental -γ̇ar, 'according to what was killed'. The closing mark is Shiratori's.

morph.gloss: to hunt in a drive (stem inferred from the Ming 圍獵) [圍獵呵]

sentences.i: so saying, he issued a decree.
sentences.n: The closing formula once more.

sentences.i: “When Sorqan-Shira said, ‘We were people of Tödöge of the Taichi'ud, indeed,’
sentences.n: A new speech, presumably Chinggis's (no speaker is named), marked by Shiratori's opening quotation mark at Sorγan-Šira; the words inside it, which Chinggis recalls, carry no marks, and the single quotes in `i` are mine. keġeġesü (Ming 說呵) is 'when (he) said'. Tödege-ji haran is 'Tödöge's people' (haran, Ming 人口, 'persons'); the ending -ji (Ming 的) stands where a genitive -jin might be expected, so the form is uncertain. ažuγ̇ui-že is a- 'to be' with a past ending -žuγ̇ui (Ming 有來) and the particle -že: 'was, indeed'. The speaker's 'we' is supplied: the verb has no person.

morph.gloss: Tödöge, a man's name [人名 的]
genitive (Ming 的; the form is uncertain)

sentences.t: Badai, Kišiliγ qojar keġeġesü Čeren-ü aduγ̇učin ažuγ̇ui-že.
sentences.l: Badai, Kišiliγ two if-they-said, Čeren-of horse-herders were-indeed.
sentences.i: and when Badai and Kishiliq, the two, said, ‘We were Cheren's horse-herders, indeed.’
sentences.n: qojar follows the two names, 'the two'. Čeren-ü is the name with the genitive -ü (Ming 的); the Ming gives only 'a name' (perhaps short for a longer one). aduγ̇učin is the horse-herder (aduγ̇un 'herd of horses' with the agent ending -či; Ming 放馬的). The verb is the same ažuγ̇ui-že as before.

sentences.t: Edöġe min-u tuluγ qorčilaγ̇ulžu ötögleġülžü darqalan žirγadqun"
sentences.l: Now my reliance bow-and-quiver-bearing-causing, cup-offering-causing, free, rejoice."
sentences.i: Now, relying on me, having (them) bear the bow and offer the cup, being free, rejoice.”
sentences.n: tuluγ (Ming 倚仗, 'rely on') is a noun or postposition, 'reliance, support'; min-u tuluγ is 'on my support'. The two causative converbs repeat the earlier unit; darqalan is a further form of darqala- (Ming 自在), 'being free'. žirγadqun is žirγa- 'to be glad' + -dqun, the polite plural command (Ming 快活您), 'rejoice (all of you)'. The closing mark is Shiratori's.

morph.gloss: to bear the bow and quiver (stem inferred from the Ming) [敎帶弓箭着]
to offer the cup (stem inferred from the Ming 喝盞) [敎喝︀盞着]
to be free, at liberty [做自在]

sentences.i: so saying, he issued a decree.
sentences.n: The closing formula, ending §219.

sentences.i: Again Chinggis Qahan said to Naya'a:
sentences.n: The opening formula, with Najaγ̇a-da, the dative-locative -da (Ming 行) on the name: 'to Naya'a'.

morph.gloss: Chinggis, the title borne by Temüjin from 1206 [太祖︀]
Naya'a, a man's name [人名 行]

sentences.t: "Širgötü ebügen Alaγ, Najaγ̇a köġüd-lüġe-ben tan-luγ̇a Tarqutai- Kiriltug-i bidan-dur barižu aisurun
sentences.l: "Širgötü old-man, Alaγ, Najaγ̇a sons-with-own you-with, Tarqutai-Kiriltuγ (acc) us-to seizing, when-coming,
sentences.i: “Old Shirgötü, with his sons Alaq and Naya'a, together with you, seizing Tarqutai-Kiriltuq for us, as you came,
sentences.n: Shiratori's opening quotation mark is on Širgötü; I take what follows as Chinggis's speech to Naya'a, closed by Shiratori's mark at ede (U57) and taken up again at U59 (opening mark supplied there). köġüd-lüġe-ben is köġü- 'son' + plural -d + the comitative -lüġe + reflexive-possessive -ben, 'with his own sons' (Ming 兒子每一同自的行); tan-luγ̇a is 'with you' (ta, stem tan-, + comitative -luγ̇a; Ming 您一同). Tarqutai- and Kiriltug-i are two printed words but one name, broken at the line end, Tarqutai-Kiriltuq, with the accusative -i. bidan-dur is bida 'we' (Ming 俺行; the Ming alternates 俺 and 咱 for this form) extended by -n- with the dative-locative -dur: 'to us'. barižu is bari- 'to seize' + converb; aisurun is aisu- 'to come' with the time converb. The grouping is as in köġud(i)-jer(i)-jen above (Sorqan-Shira, Chila'un, Chimbai): the reflexive -ben goes with the first name, so 'Old Shirgötü, with his own sons Alaq and Naya'a', which agrees with the glossary's Alaq, 'one of Shirgügetü's sons' (Shirgötü is printed here and may be the Shirgügetü of the earlier parts); why Naya'a is then also 'you' (ta, polite plural) is not clear, and the grouping is a reading, not a certainty.

morph.gloss: son [兒子每 一同自的行]
you (plural, polite; stem tan-) [您 一同]
Tarqutai-Kiriltuq, a man's name (first half, broken at the line end: Tarqutai-Kiriltug-i) [人]
second half of the name Tarqutai-Kiriltuq [名行]
to seize, take hold of [拿着]

sentences.i: on the way, arriving at Qutuqul-Nu'u,
sentences.n: žaγ̇ura is 'midway' (Ming 路間, 'on the road'); Qutuqul-Nuγ̇u-da is the place with the dative-locative -da (Ming 地名隅行); kürčü is kür- 'to reach' with the converb -čü after r.

morph.gloss: Qutuqul-Nu'u, a place name [地名隅 行]

sentences.i: there Naya'a said:
sentences.n: Naya'a speaks, in words that Chinggis relays; Shiratori marks only the outer speech, so the inner quotation marks in `i` are mine.

sentences.t: Tus qān(i)-jan ker tebčižü barižu odqun bida
sentences.l: Own-true lord-own how casting-aside seizing shall-we-go, we
sentences.i: ‘Our own true lord: how can we cast (him) aside and go, seizing (him)?’
sentences.n: tus qān(i)-jan is 'one's own rightful lord': tus 'own, rightful' (Ming 正), qān 'lord' with Shiratori's bracketed (i) and the reflexive-possessive -jan after a back vowel (Ming 主自的行); the case is the accusative or genitive. ker is 'how' (Ming 怎生). tebčižü, 'casting aside' (Ming 棄着), and barižu, 'seizing' (Ming 拿着), pull against each other; I read the question as a rhetorical 'how can we give him up and carry him off?', which fits what follows. odqun is od- 'to go' with an ending -qun (Ming 去每), and bida is 'we' (inclusive, Ming 咱). The nested speech has no marks in Shiratori.

morph.gloss: lord, ruler, khan [主 自的行]
to seize, take hold of [拿着]

sentences.i: so saying, unable to give (him) up, letting (him) go, they went away,
sentences.n: keġežü is keġe- 'to say' with the converb -žü, closing the inner speech; tebčin jadažu is 'unable to give up': tebčin (Ming 捨) is a verbal noun, 'giving up', and jada- 'to be unable' (Ming 不得着) takes the converb -žu. talbižu is talbi- 'to let go' + converb. iležü is ile- 'to send' with the Ming's 去着, 'going'. All four are converbs in a chain whose verb comes later; the subject (Naya'a and his men) is not named in it.

morph.gloss: to set down, let go [放了着]

sentences.t: Širgötü ebügen Alaγ, Najaγ̇a köġüd-lüġe-ben irežü tende
sentences.l: Širgötü old-man, Alaγ, Najaγ̇a sons-with-own coming, there
sentences.i: Old Shirgötü, with his sons Alaq and Naya'a, came, and there
sentences.n: The three names recur, grouped as before: Old Shirgötü with köġüd-lüġe-ben ('with his own sons') Alaq and Naya'a. irežü is ire- 'to come' + converb; it is the converb of this chain. tende, 'there', links to the next speech.

morph.gloss: son [兒子每 一同自的行]

sentences.i: Naya'a-Bilji'ur said:
sentences.n: Najaγ̇a-Bilžiγ̇ur (Naya'a-Bilji'ur in `i`, γ̇ as ') is printed as one name (Ming 人名); Bilžiγ̇ur looks like an added epithet and the man is evidently the same Naya'a, but I leave it as printed. The speech that follows is again unmarked.

morph.gloss: Naya'a-Biljiur, a man's name (Ming 人名; the second half perhaps an epithet) [人名]

sentences.t: Tus qān(i)-jan Tarqutai-Kiril- tug-i γartažu aisurun
sentences.i: ‘Laying hands on our own true lord, Tarqutai-Kiriltuq, as we came,
sentences.n: γartažu is from γar 'hand', 'laying a hand on' (Ming 下手着), with the converb -žu; the stem γarta- is inferred from the Ming. qān(i)-jan, the reflexive-possessive of qān 'lord', is the same word as in the last speech (here Ming 主自的行). Tarqutai-Kiril- and tug-i are the name broken at the line end again. The closing form aisurun, 'when coming', is that of the opening speech; the 'we' is mine.

morph.gloss: Tarqutai-Kiriltuq, a man's name (broken at the line end: Tarqutai-Kiril-tug-i) [人名]
the second half of the name Kiriltuq, completing it [行]
to lay hands on (from γar 'hand'; stem inferred from the Ming 下手) [下手着]

sentences.i: yet unable to give (him) up, we let (him) go and went away,
sentences.n: žiči (Ming 郤, 'but, yet') turns the sentence; the four converbs are those of the speech above (tebčin jadažu talbižu iležü), now with 'we' as subject.

morph.gloss: to set down, let go [放了着]

sentences.t: ba Čiṅgis Qaγ̇an-a küčü ögüre irebe.
sentences.l: we Chinggis Qaγan-to strength to-give came.
sentences.i: we came to give our strength to Chinggis Qahan.
sentences.n: ba is 'we' here (Ming 俺); as a form it leaves the listener out, against bida 咱, though the Ming itself alternates 俺 and 咱 for the bida forms. Qaγ̇an-a has the dative-locative -a (Ming 行), 'to'. ögüre is ög- 'to give' with a linking vowel and -re, a converb of purpose (Ming 與), 'in order to give'; küčü is 'strength' (Ming 氣力). The finite verb irebe, 'came', closes the long chain of converbs.

morph.gloss: Chinggis, the title borne by Temüjin from 1206 [太祖︀]
converb of purpose: in order to

sentences.i: if we had come having laid hands on our own lord,
sentences.n: qān(i)-jan again, with γartažu 'laying hands' and ireġesü, ire- 'to come' + the conditional -ġesü (Ming 來呵), 'if (we) came'. Ming 皇帝自的行 for the lord here suggests the lord is the 'emperor' in the Ming translator's eyes.

morph.gloss: to lay hands on (from γar 'hand'; stem inferred from the Ming 下手) [下手着]

sentences.t: tus qān(i)-jan γartaγsad haran mönö qoina ker itegegdekün ede"
sentences.l: own-true lord-own hand-layers people hereafter how to-be-relied-on, these"
sentences.i: the people who laid hands on their own true lord, how will these be relied on, hereafter?’”
sentences.n: tus qān(i)-jan again; γartaγsad is γarta- + the past participle -γsan + plural -d, 'those who laid hands' (Ming 下手的每). haran is 'people'. mönö qoina is 'hereafter' (qoina 'after', Ming 後; mönö, Ming 久, 'long'). itegegdekün is itege- 'to trust, rely on' + the passive -gde- + an ending -kün (Ming 倚仗每), 'be relied on'; ede is 'these' (Ming 這每). Shiratori's closing quotation mark stands here, at ede, although Chinggis goes on: the mark seems to close the inner speech or to be a slip; in `i` I keep it as printed.

morph.gloss: lord, ruler, khan [主 自的行]
to lay hands on (from γar 'hand'; stem inferred from the Ming 下手) [下手的每]
to trust, rely on (stem inferred from the Ming 倚仗) [倚仗每]

sentences.i: so they would be spoken of, he said.
sentences.n: keġegdekün is keġe- 'to say' + the passive -gde- + -kün, as itegegdekün just before: 'be spoken of, be called' (Ming 被說每). keġežüġü is the past narrative -žüġü (Ming 說有), 'said'. I take the two words as Naya'a-Bilji'ur's close, 'they will say this of us', but they may belong to the narration; the grammar leaves it open.

sentences.i: “When he said, ‘I could not give up my own lord,’ then
sentences.n: Shiratori has no opening quotation mark before this passage, only a closing one at the end (at medetügei, below); `i` supplies the opening here and I take what follows to the end as Chinggis's own words. Qān(i)-jan is the same 'own lord' as above (capital Q, for it begins the clause). tebčin jadaba is jada- 'to be unable' in the past -ba (Ming 捨不能了). kēġesü is keġe- 'to say' + the conditional with the long vowel Shiratori prints (Ming 說呵), 'when (he) said'.

morph.gloss: lord, ruler, khan [皇帝 自的行]

sentences.t: tus qān(i)-jan tebčin jadaγsan josu jeke töre-ji sedkižüġüi keġen
sentences.l: own-true lord-own giving-up not-able-one principle great law (acc) it-was-thought, saying,
sentences.i: ‘Not being able to give up one's own true lord: that principle I held a great law,’ so thinking,
sentences.n: tebčin jadaγsan is 'one who could not give up' (jada- + the past participle -γsan; Ming 捨不得了); josu is 'rule, principle' (Ming 理), jeke 'great', töre-ji is töre 'law, order' (Ming 理) with the accusative -ji (Ming 行). sedkižüġüi is sedki- 'to think' with the past narrative ending -žüġüi (Ming 想了有), 'was thought', then keġen 'saying'. The verb carries no person; 'I' is chosen because the speech is Chinggis's, 'his words' (in-ü) are Naya'a's, and the next unit has the first-person tüšije. Who holds the thought is a reading.

morph.gloss: lord, ruler, khan [主 自的行]
past participle: the one who could not
law, order, right way [理 行]

sentences.i: approving his words,
sentences.n: üge is 'word, speech'; in-ü is the third-person genitive, 'his', set after its noun (Ming 他的). žöbšiježü is žöbšije- (probably žöbšiye-) 'to approve, assent' (Ming 道是着, 'saying yes') with the converb.

morph.gloss: his, her, its (third-person genitive, set after its noun) [他的]
to approve, assent (Ming 道是) [道是着]

sentences.i: ‘Let me entrust (you) with one task,’ I said.
sentences.n: nigen üile-dür is 'in one matter' (üile 'work, deed' + dative-locative -dür; Ming 勾當裏). tüšije is tüši- 'to entrust, set on' (Ming 委付咱, 'let us entrust') with a first-person optative -je. keġeleġei: keġe- 'to say' + -leġei, which I met in a question, 'did you say?'; the Ming here has 說來 without 麽, so I take it as plain past, 'said'. The 'I' rests on the first-person -je (Ming 咱), not on any pronoun.

morph.gloss: to entrust, set on (stem inferred from the Ming 委付) [委付咱]

sentences.t: Edöġe Boγ̇orču-da baraγ̇un γar-un tümen medetügei;
sentences.l: Now Boγ̇orču-to right hand-of ten-thousand let-him-have-charge;
sentences.i: Now, Bo'orchu: let him have charge of the right-hand tümen, the ten thousand;
sentences.n: Edöġe 'now'; Boγ̇orču-da has the dative-locative -da (Ming 行). baraγ̇un γar-un is 'of the right hand' (baraγ̇un 'right', γar 'hand' + genitive -un), qualifying tümen, the unit of ten thousand (Ming 萬戶, 'ten thousand households'). medetügei is mede- 'to know, manage' + the optative -tügei (Ming 敎管者), 'let him have charge of'.

morph.gloss: Bo'orchu, a man's name [人名 行]
ten thousand; a division of ten thousand households [萬戶]
to know; here to have charge of [敎管者︀]

sentences.t: Muqali-da γuowaṅ nere ögčü žeġün γar-un tümen medeġülbe.
sentences.l: Muqali-to Guowang name giving, left hand-of ten-thousand caused-to-manage.
sentences.i: and giving Muqali the title Guowang, he put the left-hand tümen in his charge.
sentences.n: Γuowaṅ is the Chinese title 國王 'prince of the state', written in the Ming's own characters, and nere (Ming 名分) is 'name, title, rank': 'the title Guowang'. ögčü is ög- 'to give' with the converb -čü after a consonant. medeġülbe is mede- 'to know, manage' + the causative -ġül- + past -be (Ming 敎管了), 'had (him) manage'; žeġün is 'left'. Compare the right-hand tümen in the unit before.

morph.gloss: Guowang, the Chinese title 國王 'prince of the state' [(國王)]
ten thousand; a division of ten thousand households [萬戶]
to know; here to have charge of [敎管了]

sentences.i: Now Naya'a: let him have charge of the middle tümen.”
sentences.n: tüb-ün is tüb 'middle, centre' with the genitive -ün (Ming 中的), 'of the middle'; the third tümen. Najaγ̇a stands without a case ending here (Ming 名), though the sense is the same as for Bo'orchu. The closing quotation mark is Shiratori's.

morph.gloss: ten thousand; a division of ten thousand households [萬戶]
to know; here to have charge of [敎管者︀]

sentences.i: so saying, he issued a decree.
sentences.n: The closing formula, ending §220.

sentences.t: Basa "Žebe Sübeġetei qojar öġer-ün oluγsad žüġegseġer(i)-jen miṅγalatuγai" keġebe.
sentences.l: Again: "Žebe, Sübeġetei two own-of those-got, those-set-own let-them-make-a-thousand," he-said.
sentences.i: Again: “Jebe and Sübegetei, the two: of the men they have gained and set in place themselves, let them make a thousand,” he said.
sentences.n: The hardest clause here is the string öġer-ün oluγsad žüġegseġer(i)-jen miṅγalatuγai. öġer-ün is 'of one's own' (öġer 'own' + genitive -ün); oluγsad is ol- 'to get' + the past participle -γsan + plural -d (Ming 得了的每), 'those got'; žüġegseġer(i)-jen is built on žüġe- 'to set in place' (Ming 置了的; stem inferred), in a past-participle form whose ending I have not analysed, with the reflexive-possessive -jen. miṅγalatuγai is miṅγala- 'to make a thousand' (from miṅγa) + the optative -tuγai (Ming 千戶做者). I read: 'let them form a thousand out of the men they have gained and arranged'. Sübeġetei is printed in full (Sübegetei in `i`, not Sübegei); qojar follows the two names. The ending of žüġegseġer(i)-jen may be the participle -gsen plus the instrumental -ġer, as in oluγsaγ̇ar, but the Ming (置了的 自的行) gives no 'according to', so I leave it unanalysed. The marks are Shiratori's.

morph.gloss: to set in place (stem inferred from the Ming 置) [置了的 自的行]
to make a thousand (from miṅγa) [千戶做者︀]

sentences.t: Basa Degei Qoniči-da bügdeġül-i čiγ̇ulγažu miṅγa medeġülbe.
sentences.l: Again Degei shepherd-to, bügdeġül (acc) having-caused-to-gather, thousand caused-to-manage.
sentences.i: Again, Degei the shepherd, gathering the bügdeġül, was put in charge of a thousand.
sentences.n: Qoniči-da is qoniči 'shepherd' (qoni 'sheep' + agent -či; Ming 牧羊的) with the dative-locative -da (Ming 行), as Degei's title and also the case of the one put in charge: 'Degei the shepherd'. bügdeġül-i has the accusative -i; the Ming reads it 理沒行, 'those without order', and the word is otherwise unknown to me. I leave it as printed. čiγ̇ulγažu is the causative converb, 'making gather'; miṅγa is 'a thousand'; medeġülbe is 'had (him) manage' as in §220. The unit-of-a-thousand grant resembles that to Jebe and Sübegetei just before.

morph.gloss: unknown word (Ming 理沒; sense uncertain) [理沒行]
to gather, assemble (stem inferred from the Ming 聚) [敎聚着]
to know; here to have charge of [敎管了]

sentences.i: Again, to Küchügur the carpenter:
sentences.n: modoči is mod 'wood' + the agent ending -či (Ming 木匠, 'carpenter'), with the dative-locative -da (Ming 行). Küčügür is a man's name (Ming 人名), the same letters as küčügür 'field-mouse' in the glossary. No colon follows; the speech begins in the next unit.

sentences.i: “(Your) people being short, levying (men) from here and from there,
sentences.n: Shiratori's opening quotation mark is on Irge. irge is 'people' (Ming 百姓), a form of irgen. datuγdažu is a converb of a verb 'to lack' made passive (Ming 被缺着, 'being short of'; the stem datuγ- is inferred from the Ming). endēče and tendēče are the ablatives of ene 'this' and tende 'there', 'from here', 'from there' (the long vowel is Shiratori's). qubčižu is qubči- 'to levy, gather in' (Ming 收拾着). 'Your' is supplied from the sense.

morph.gloss: to be short, lacking (stem inferred from the Ming 缺) [被缺着]

sentences.i: from the Jadaran, Mulqalqu came duly as (your) companion.
sentences.n: Žadaran-ača is the clan with the ablative -ača, 'from the Jadaran'. žüki-jer is žüki (Ming 正, 'right, proper') with the ending -jer, which has the shape of the instrumental, so 'duly, by right'. nököčelüġe is nököče- 'to be a companion' (from nökör 'companion'; the glossary's nököče-) with the ending -lüġe (Ming 做伴來, 'came as companion'), the same shape as keġeleġei and the glossary's kelelüġe. The ending's analysis is a guess.

morph.gloss: the Jadaran, a clan name [種名處]
right, proper (Ming 正) [正 依着]
to be a companion (from nökör 'companion'; stem inferred from the Ming) [做伴來]
past ending (uncertain; Ming 來), as in keġeleġei and the glossary's kelelüġe

sentences.i: Küchügur and Mulqalqu, the two, together making a thousand,
sentences.n: qojar follows the two names. nigen-e is nigen 'one' with the dative-locative -e (Ming 一行), 'in one, together'. minγalažu is miṅγala- 'to make a thousand' + converb, as in the last section's miṅγalatuγai.

morph.gloss: to make a thousand (from miṅγa) [千戶做着]

sentences.i: consulting together, stay,” he said.
sentences.n: ejetüldüžü is a converb (-žü) of a stem ejetüldü- (Ming 商量着, 'consulting'); I take it as 'conferring with each other', but the analysis is uncertain. adqun is the Ming's 住您, 'stay (you all)': a- 'to be, stay' with a plural mark -d- and the polite command -qun; both are tentative. The closing mark is Shiratori's, and keġebe ends §223 and the part.

morph.gloss: to consult together (Ming 商量; analysis uncertain) [商量着]
